questions.question_text: What is the core of design thinking?
questions.explanation: Design thinking is fundamentally a human-centric approach to problem-solving. It prioritizes the needs and experiences of the human behind the problem over merely focusing on the product or immediate profitability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following highlights a problem with the Stage-gate model?
questions.explanation: The traditional Stage-gate model is linear and typically jumps straight from a known problem to an idea or solution. This makes it rigid and prone to failure when faced with complex, unpredictable human challenges.

questions.question_text: What is more important in design thinking?
questions.explanation: Understanding 'Why to solve a problem?' provides the inspiration and true intent behind the process. It is infinitely more important than the technical 'How' because it ensures you are solving the right problem.

questions.question_text: What is a crucial starting point to keep in mind during the ideation stage?

options.A: Coming up with many average ideas
options.B: Coming up with few average ideas
options.C: Coming up with few good ideas
options.D: Coming up with many good ideas

questions.explanation: A core rule of ideation is that quantity drives quality. Generating a massive volume of average ideas initially is the best way to eventually filter down to a few exceptionally good ones.

questions.question_text: Which movement of Gandhi's is comparable to prototype stage?

options.A: The train incident in South Africa
options.C: When first Indian National Congress was formed

questions.explanation: The Dandi March served as a prototype for Mahatma Gandhi's design thinking. It allowed him to test the concept of non-violent civil disobedience on a small, focused scale (salt) before scaling it nationwide.

questions.question_text: Lateral thinking works in the realm of
questions.explanation: Lateral thinking is best used when the problem is Known but the solution is Unknown, as it involves creative workarounds and sideways thinking to discover a new approach.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a condition under which design thinking is used?
questions.explanation: Design thinking requires five key conditions to be effective: Audacity of Goal, Ambiguity of Context, Availability of Time, Access to Customers, and Diversity of the Team.

questions.question_text: Which of the following must be cultivated to adopt a design thinking mindset? (Choose all that apply)

options.B: Knowing everything about something / Deeply thinking about anything that comes to mind

questions.explanation: The three essential attributes of a design thinker's mindset are a Clear Head (knowing priorities), a Deep Heart (compassion/empathy), and a Thick Skin (indifference to unwarranted opinions).

questions.question_text: It is necessary to

options.A: To say No to increase our Zone of influence
options.B: To say Yes to increase our Zone of Influence
options.C: To say No to increase our Zone of concern
options.D: To say Yes to increase our Zone of concern

questions.explanation: To maintain a clear head, you must shrink your limitless 'Zone of Concern' by saying 'No', and actively expand your actionable 'Zone of Influence' by saying 'Yes'.

questions.question_text: Doctors try to understand the issue till its
questions.explanation: Unlike pharmacists who provide quick fixes for symptoms, doctors map out symptoms to identify and treat the actual underlying root causes, yielding high-value results.

questions.question_text: To look at a problem from an objective lens, it is necessary to think about it from the level of
questions.explanation: To truly evaluate a problem's gravity and gain objective emotional space, the 'Pay Grade Rule' suggests you should think two levels above your pay grade (your boss's boss).

questions.question_text: Which of these is not a component to be considered while developing a design brief?
questions.explanation: A good design brief acts as a sandbox. It must be Inspirational, Constrained, and Vague enough to allow creative freedom. Rigidity restricts the creative exploration required.

questions.question_text: For an idea to be termed as creative, it needs to be
questions.explanation: Creativity is scientifically defined as the ability to generate an idea that is simultaneously novel (new/unique) and useful (valuable/practical).

questions.question_text: In the Alternative Uses Test, which of these is not one of the parameters used in measuring creativity?
questions.explanation: Guilford's Alternate Uses Test measures creativity using four parameters: Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration. Accuracy is associated with convergent thinking (intelligence).

questions.question_text: Taking hobbies seriously helps one

options.B: get exposed to different perspectives in life
options.C: get exposed to different kinds of people in life

questions.explanation: Cultivating hobbies nurtures creativity by building self-confidence, offering diverse perspectives, building new networks, and encouraging cross-domain associative thinking.

questions.question_text: There is creativity involved in humour.
questions.explanation: True. Humor and creativity share identical neural circuitry. Both rely on establishing a linear setup and then suddenly breaking the pattern with a benign violation of logic.

questions.question_text: An important point to be noted about judgement during ideation is that

options.A: we must critically judge an idea or situation
options.C: we do not need to care about it
options.D: judgement must be present all the time

questions.explanation: During the ideation phase, judgment must be strictly deferred. Evaluating ideas while attempting to generate them causes evaluation apprehension and kills creative momentum.

questions.question_text: Business viability refers to

options.A: Having the technological base to finish the project
options.D: Understanding the needs of the consumer

questions.explanation: In the Innovation Trinity, Business Viability specifically addresses whether the proposed solution makes economic and commercial sense for the organization to pursue.

questions.question_text: Why is prototyping necessary?
questions.explanation: Prototyping brings ideas to life. It offers spatial clarity, identifies hidden constraints early to prevent massive failures, and provides visual confidence to stakeholders and customers.

questions.question_text: Which of these is not a rule of prototyping?

options.B: Maximising learning per unit time and dollar
options.D: Don't show your best product till the end

questions.explanation: Prototyping encourages showing rough, quick-and-dirty models early on. Hiding your work until it is 'perfect' contradicts the rapid feedback loop fundamental to design thinking.

questions.question_text: Which of these is not a service prototyping method?
questions.explanation: Lego and clay are physical, spatial materials used for Product Prototyping. Storyboarding, SCQA storytelling, and scenarios are temporal methods used for Service Prototyping.

questions.question_text: The business model canvas begins with
questions.explanation: The Business Model Canvas centers entirely around the Value Proposition—the core functional and emotional offering that the business promises to deliver to its users.
